title: May the Psalms Be With You
description: Seven categories of pure chaos: Forrest Frank, weird animals, more Narnia, Star Wars, martial arts films, Marvel heroes, and the ancient tweets known as the Book of Psalms.

questions.question: Before becoming a Christian music sensation, Forrest Frank was one half of this feel-good pop duo whose 2019 hit 'Sunday Best' peaked at #19 on the Billboard Hot 100.
This 2023 Forrest Frank collaboration with rapper Hulvey became his viral Christian debut — racking up over 60 million Spotify streams and appearing in every worship playlist seemingly overnight.

This bouncy Forrest Frank track became the go-to TikTok sound for creators projecting maximum positive energy in 2024, hitting #2 on Hot Christian Songs and earning him the Dove Award New Artist of the Year.

Forrest Frank's 2024 album 'Child of God' earned a nomination from the music industry's most prestigious awards ceremony for Best Contemporary Christian Music Album — the first major recognition of his solo career.
When Elton John spent the COVID pandemic recording collaborations with various artists, he teamed up with Forrest Frank's pop duo Surfaces on a song called 'Learn to Fly' for this 2021 album.
This egg-laying, duck-billed, venomous Australian mammal looks like it was designed by a committee that couldn't agree on anything — and frankly, that tracks.
With the ability to punch at bullet speed and see 16 types of color, this small ocean crustacean is either the most equipped creature in the sea or deeply overcompensating.
Guinness World Records officially named this scrappy little African mammal the 'world's most fearless animal' — it eats venomous cobras, steals food from lions, and simply does not care.

This microscopic 'water bear' has been boiled, frozen, irradiated, and shot into open space — surviving all of it — making it the most indestructible life form on Earth that you could accidentally vacuum up.

When this tiny shrimp snaps its claw shut, the resulting cavitation bubble briefly reaches temperatures rivaling the surface of the sun — which is impressive for something you could lose in a fish tank.

Edmund Pevensie's entire moral collapse in 'The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe' can be traced to this magically addictive candy the White Witch used to bribe him — proof that sugar is genuinely dangerous.

This half-human, half-goat Narnian was the first resident Lucy met after entering Narnia — carrying parcels, hosting her for tea, and briefly serving as a White Witch informant before having a change of heart.

Often described as the most insufferable child in the Narnia series, this Pevensie cousin transforms into a dragon in 'The Voyage of the Dawn Treader' — a development many readers quietly considered an improvement.

When the White Witch's power begins to crumble, this legendary gift-giver suddenly appears in the snowy Narnian wood to hand out presents to the Pevensie children — the clearest possible sign that things were finally looking up.

C.S. Lewis's decision to load Narnia with Christian allegory reportedly frustrated this fellow Oxford friend — who preferred immersive world-building over symbolism and helped found the literary group called the Inklings.
This small, green, 900-year-old Jedi Master chooses to live in a swamp on the planet Dagobah and speaks in a word order that is reversed, he does — and somehow this makes him seem wise.

Pilot of the Millennium Falcon and self-described scoundrel, this famous smuggler once boasted his ship made the Kessel Run in fewer than 12 parsecs — a unit of distance, not time, which nobody seemed brave enough to correct.

The Rebel Alliance's secret base on this frozen, miserable planet was discovered by the Empire within the first twenty minutes of 'The Empire Strikes Back,' proving glaciers are a terrible hiding spot.
This mild-mannered Galactic Senator spent decades secretly being the most powerful Sith Lord in history, operating as Darth Sidious while everyone around him apparently missed all the obvious signs.

Introduced in 'The Phantom Menace,' these tiny microorganisms inside cells were George Lucas's scientific explanation for Force sensitivity — a concept Star Wars fans have spent 25 years politely trying to forget.

The revolutionary training methods of polishing cars, painting fences, and sanding floors were Mr. Miyagi's secretly brilliant karate curriculum for bullied teenager Daniel LaRusso in this 1984 classic.
This Hong Kong martial arts legend died at age 32 in 1973 — just weeks before his most famous film, 'Enter the Dragon,' was released — leaving behind a career that defined an entire genre.

A Hong Kong detective's pinpoint martial precision combined with his partner's unstoppable talking speed in this 1998 buddy-cop film — creating the perfect equation of punching and comedic cultural misunderstanding.

Directed by Ang Lee, this 2000 film featured gravity-defying wire-work combat, a flying magical sword, and Michelle Yeoh — and became the highest-grossing foreign-language film ever released in the United States at the time.
questions.answer: What is Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon?

questions.question: Jean-Claude Van Damme stars as an American soldier competing in a secret underground full-contact tournament in this 1988 film — loosely based on the allegedly fabricated autobiography of one Frank Dux.

This super-soldier Avenger — Steve Rogers — was injected with an experimental serum, frozen in ice for 70 years, and woke up in modern times still somehow the most morally upstanding person in any room.

When physicist Bruce Banner gets even slightly upset, he transforms into a very large, very green Avenger who communicates primarily through structural damage and whose health insurance must be astronomical.

This wise-cracking Marvel antihero — played by Ryan Reynolds — can regenerate from virtually any wound, refuses to stop making jokes, and regularly breaks the fourth wall to remind everyone this is a movie.
This adamantium-clawed X-Man — who goes by Logan — cannot age, rarely stays dead, and finally received a beautiful and absolutely devastating farewell in the 2017 film bearing his alias.

Once a brilliant but arrogant neurosurgeon, this Marvel hero suffered a career-ending car accident, journeyed to Nepal, and returned as the Sorcerer Supreme — complete with a sentient cape that has its own opinions.
This most-memorized Bible passage, opening with 'The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want,' has appeared on more sympathy cards, graduation speeches, and tattoo sleeves than any other scripture.

After his affair with Bathsheba and the arranged death of her husband Uriah, King David wrote this chapter as a deeply personal prayer of repentance — essentially the ancient world's most elaborate public apology.
At 176 verses organized alphabetically across all 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet, this is the longest single chapter in the entire Bible — a commitment to thoroughness that truly goes hard.

Opening with the anguished cry 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me,' this chapter was directly quoted by Jesus on the cross in both Matthew and Mark — making it the most prophetically precise passage in the Old Testament.

The Book of Psalms closes with this chapter's exuberant command to praise God using every instrument available — cymbals, trumpets, harps, and lyres — ending with the ultimate mic drop: 'Let everything that has breath praise the Lord.'
